title: criterion-add-spec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> criterion add <spec.json>` and of the `criterion add` apply op — ONE document uniqueness criterion in the exact shape A12 stores it in `content.documentUniquenessCriteria`, so an entry returned by `criterion read` is a valid spec. A criterion names fields whose values no two stored documents may share; it is model data only, and no rule, computation or document validation evaluates it. The spec demands a `name`, because `criterion read`/`remove` address a criterion by it, and a name the model already uses is refused (RK_NAME_EXISTS). It also closes every object and demands `fullName`, `locale` and `text` in their items, though A12 reads past an unknown member and skips a field item without `fullName`: those are typo guards, since a misspelled member would otherwise vanish silently and leave a criterion over fewer fields than written. What A12 admits is its consistency check's to decide, in its own sentence (KERNEL-FINDINGS KF671 lists the classes): among them, each field must be required, persisted and outside any repeatable group and named by its full path, and each model locale needs a text whose `$path$` parameters name only the criterion's fields.

name.description: the criterion's name, unique within the model; `criterion read <name>` and `criterion remove <name>` address it by this

fields.description: the fields whose combined values must be unique across stored documents, in order

errorMessage.description: the error text per locale, one entry for every locale the model declares

locale.description: a locale code the model declares, e.g. en_US

text.description: the message; a `$/Full/Path.value$` parameter may name only one of the criterion's own fields
